chapter_summary: Jesus calls Himself the true vine and teaches His disciples to remain in Him, bear fruit, love one another, and expect opposition. He promises the Spirit of truth, who will testify about Him.
main_lesson: Life and lasting fruit come through relationship with Jesus. His disciples respond to His already-given love by loving one another and bearing truthful witness, even when others oppose them.

memory_verse.kjv: This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you.
memory_verse.little_bible: This is my commandment: that you love one another, as I have loved you.

parent_guide: Access: default for ages 6–8 and 9–12 with adult context; ages 3–5 receive only curated verses such as 1, 4–5, 9, 11–12, and 17. Sensitivity: judgment and burning imagery, death and self-sacrifice, rejection, hatred, persecution, guilt, religious difference, prayer expectations, obedience, and complex teaching about the Holy Spirit. Never use pruning or burning to frighten children or explain abuse and suffering as improvement. Verse 13 points toward Jesus’ voluntary death and never endorses self-harm or unsafe sacrifice. Prayer promises are shaped by remaining in Jesus and His words, not magic or guaranteed outcomes. Obedience responds to love and never authorizes unsafe adult demands. Persecution teaching supports truth and help-seeking, not victimhood. The Spirit testifies about Jesus and must not be presented as private voices children must obey.
application_for_children: Children can learn to depend on Jesus, notice the good fruit His love grows, practise love with safe boundaries, pray without treating prayer as magic, and tell the truth about Jesus. Children may always ask questions, pass on sensitive discussion, refuse harmful instructions, and seek help from trusted safe adults.

verses.kjv: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.
verses.little_bible: I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus is the true vine. His Father is the gardener.
verses.meaning: Jesus uses a living metaphor: he is the true vine and the Father is the cultivator. It describes relationship and dependence, not a physical plant or a test of a child’s worth.
verses.prayer: Jesus, keep me connected to you.
verses.discussion_question: What does the vine picture help you understand about Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Look at a vine picture and discuss what depends on what.
verses.do_it_today: Optionally draw a vine joined to healthy branches.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:1, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.
verses.little_bible: Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he takes away: and every branch that bears fruit, he prunes it, that it may bear more fruit.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Father removes branches with no fruit. He prunes fruitful branches so they grow more fruit.
verses.meaning: The gardening image pictures the Father’s purposeful care and judgment. “Pruning” must not be used to label abuse, illness, or punishment as God hurting a child to improve them.
verses.prayer: Father, help me receive your wise care.
verses.discussion_question: How can caring guidance help something grow without causing harm?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss the difference between helpful correction and harmful treatment.
verses.do_it_today: Help care gently for a safe household plant.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:2, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.
verses.little_bible: Now you are clean through the word which I have spoken to you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus’ word had made the disciples clean.
verses.meaning: Jesus declares the disciples clean through his received word. Cleanness here is relational and spiritual, not bodily hygiene, perfection, or freedom from future mistakes.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for your restoring word.
verses.discussion_question: What kind of cleanness is Jesus describing?
verses.family_discussion: Name ways Jesus’ words bring restoration rather than perfectionism.
verses.do_it_today: Hear Jesus’ words again and rest without trying to be perfect.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:3, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
verses.little_bible: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you unless you remain in me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, ‘Stay joined to me, and I will remain in you, like a branch joined to its vine.’
verses.meaning: Remaining in Jesus is the source of fruitful discipleship, as a branch depends on its vine. It is not physical merging and does not mean anxious effort to keep Jesus from abandoning a child.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me remain close to you.
verses.discussion_question: What helps a branch stay alive and fruitful?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about practices that help your family attend to Jesus without pressure.
verses.do_it_today: Choose a quiet way to attend to Jesus today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:4, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
verses.little_bible: I am the vine, you are the branches: The one who remains in me, and I in him, that person bears much fruit: for without me you can do nothing.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus is the vine, and his disciples are branches. They bear fruit by staying joined to him; apart from him they cannot bear this fruit.
verses.meaning: Jesus identifies disciples as dependent branches. “Nothing” concerns fruit-bearing apart from him, not a claim that children have no abilities, dignity, or value.
verses.prayer: Jesus, grow good fruit in your people.
verses.discussion_question: How can depending on Jesus differ from thinking you are worthless?
verses.family_discussion: Affirm each person’s God-given value while discussing dependence on Christ.
verses.do_it_today: Ask an adult to point out one gift they see in you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:5, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
verses.little_bible: If a person does not remain in me, he is thrown out like a branch and withers; and people gather them, throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A branch apart from the vine withers and is burned.
verses.meaning: The withered branch and fire form a serious judgment image. Christians variously relate it to false disciples, apostasy, final judgment, or severe discipline. The verse must never be used as a graphic threat to force a child’s behaviour or profession of faith.
verses.prayer: God, give us wisdom with difficult warnings.
verses.discussion_question: What questions does this serious image raise? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Let an adult explain the fire image calmly, or skip it for younger children.
verses.do_it_today: With an adult, name this as a serious warning that must never be used to frighten or control you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:6, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.
verses.little_bible: If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, you will ask whatever you desire, and it will be done for you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, ‘If you remain in me and my words remain in you, you may ask, and I will answer.’
verses.meaning: This prayer promise belongs to remaining in Jesus and having his words shape desire. It is not a magic formula or guarantee that every request—including safety, healing, or success—will happen.
verses.prayer: Jesus, shape my prayers by your words.
verses.discussion_question: How might Jesus’ words shape what someone asks for?
verses.family_discussion: Compare a wish list with prayer shaped by Jesus’ words.
verses.do_it_today: If you wish, shape one request using Jesus’ teaching. You may pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:7, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.
verses.little_bible: In this my Father is glorified: that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Fruitful disciples bring glory to the Father.
verses.meaning: Fruitful lives display the Father’s goodness and mark discipleship. Fruit should be explained as Christ-shaped life and witness, not scores, productivity, or earning divine approval.
verses.prayer: Father, let my life honor you.
verses.discussion_question: What kind of fruit could show God’s goodness?
verses.family_discussion: Choose one fruit such as patience, truth, or generosity to notice this week.
verses.do_it_today: Choose one small act of patient or generous fruit.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:8, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love.
verses.little_bible: As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you: remain in my love.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, “Stay in the love I give you.”
verses.meaning: The Son’s love for disciples reflects the Father’s love for the Son. Remaining in love means living within a relationship already given, not earning affection.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me rest in your love.
verses.discussion_question: What might remaining in Jesus’ love look like?
verses.family_discussion: Describe love that stays present without controlling another person.
verses.do_it_today: Receive a safe hug if you want one, or choose another sign of care.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:9, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.
verses.little_bible: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and remain in his love.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus connected keeping his commands with remaining in his love.
verses.meaning: Jesus’ obedience to the Father models loving faithfulness. Keeping Jesus’ commands responds to love; it does not earn love or authorize harmful, secretive, or unsafe adult demands.
verses.prayer: Jesus, teach me safe and loving obedience.
verses.discussion_question: Why is obedience a response to love rather than its price?
verses.family_discussion: Repeat the safety rule: no adult may demand harmful obedience or secrets.
verses.do_it_today: Practise saying, “That instruction feels unsafe; I will tell someone.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:10, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
verses.little_bible: These things have I spoken to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be full.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus wanted his joy to fill the disciples.
verses.meaning: Jesus teaches so his own joy may dwell in the disciples and mature fully. Full joy is not compulsory cheerfulness and can coexist with grief or fear.
verses.prayer: Jesus, let your joy grow in me.
verses.discussion_question: How can joy and sadness exist together?
verses.family_discussion: Share a time joy was present during a difficult season, with permission to pass.
verses.do_it_today: Make space for one joyful activity without forcing a mood.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:11, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you.
verses.little_bible: This is my commandment: that you love one another, as I have loved you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus commanded them to love as he loved.
verses.meaning: Jesus makes his self-giving love the pattern for mutual love. Love includes truth and safe boundaries; it never requires access for an unsafe person.
verses.prayer: Jesus, teach us love with truth and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can love include a safe boundary?
verses.family_discussion: Practise a kind “no” that protects a healthy boundary.
verses.do_it_today: Offer help and respect the other person’s answer.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:12, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
verses.little_bible: Greater love has no one than this, that a person lay down his life for his friends.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus described giving one’s life for friends as the greatest love.
verses.meaning: Jesus anticipates his voluntary death for his friends. This uniquely points toward the cross and must never be used to praise self-harm, suicide, dangerous dares, or a child sacrificing personal safety.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for giving yourself willingly.
verses.discussion_question: Why must this verse never encourage self-harm or danger? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: State clearly that seeking death or injury is never a way to obey this verse.
verses.do_it_today: If this verse brings up thoughts of harming yourself, stop and tell a trusted safe adult right away. You never need to describe those thoughts to the app.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:13, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.
verses.little_bible: You are my friends, if you do whatever I command you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus called obedient disciples his friends.
verses.meaning: Jesus calls the disciples friends in connection with following his commands. Friendship with Jesus is grace-filled relationship, not a reward children earn through perfect compliance.
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for calling disciples friends.
verses.discussion_question: How is friendship with Jesus different from earning approval?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how grace comes before faithful response.
verses.do_it_today: Thank Jesus for friendship without listing achievements.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:14, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.
verses.little_bible: I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know what his master does. But I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything I heard from my Father.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus called them friends and shared the Father’s teaching with them.
verses.meaning: Unlike servants kept uninformed, the disciples are called friends and receive what Jesus heard from the Father. This does not erase Jesus’ authority or make every private thought a divine message.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me listen to what you reveal.
verses.discussion_question: Why might sharing truth show friendship?
verses.family_discussion: Compare a distant master with a friend who explains his purpose.
verses.do_it_today: Share one helpful truth with someone who wants to hear it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:15, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
verses.little_bible: You have not chosen me, but I have chosen you and appointed you, so that you should go and bear fruit, and so that your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, ‘You did not choose me; I chose and sent you to bear lasting fruit. Ask the Father in my name, and he may answer.’
verses.meaning: Jesus first addresses the apostles: his choice and appointment precede their going and lasting fruit. Christians differ on how this apostolic choosing relates to divine election and human response. Prayer remains shaped by Jesus’ name and mission, not a promise of any desired outcome.
verses.prayer: Jesus, grow lasting fruit through your people.
verses.discussion_question: What comes first here: Jesus’ choice or the disciples’ fruit?
verses.family_discussion: Trace Jesus’ choosing, sending, fruit, and prayer in the verse.
verses.do_it_today: Draw fruit that lasts, such as kindness remembered.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:16, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: These things I command you, that ye love one another.
verses.little_bible: These things I command you, that you love one another.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus commanded them to love one another.
verses.meaning: The repeated command centers the community on mutual love. Love is not coercion, secrecy, forced touch, or return to an unsafe relationship.
verses.prayer: Jesus, teach us to love one another.
verses.discussion_question: What is one safe way people can love one another?
verses.family_discussion: Plan one safe act of care that expects no reward.
verses.do_it_today: Choose an optional act of love with safe boundaries.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:17, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.
verses.little_bible: If the world hates you, you know that it hated me before it hated you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, ‘If the world hates you, remember it hated me first.’
verses.meaning: Jesus prepares disciples for hostility by reminding them he faced it first. This comforts persecuted believers but must not teach children to accept bullying, abuse, or victimhood instead of seeking help.
verses.prayer: Jesus, comfort people who face hatred.
verses.discussion_question: What should a child do when someone shows hatred or bullying? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Name trusted adults who can help with bullying; no disclosure is required.
verses.do_it_today: Write down two trusted adults who help with bullying, or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:18, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.
verses.little_bible: If you were of the world, the world would love his own: but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus chose his disciples out of the world. Because they did not belong to it, the world hated them.
verses.meaning: The “world” here means human society organized in resistance to Jesus, not every non-Christian person. Distinctive discipleship never permits contempt, isolation, or assuming all disagreement is hatred.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help us be faithful and respectful.
verses.discussion_question: Why does “the world” not mean every person outside church?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how Christians can be distinct while respecting every neighbour.
verses.do_it_today: With an adult, greet a known safe person whose beliefs differ from yours.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:19, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also.
verses.little_bible: Remember the word that I said to you, The servant is not greater than his master. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said some would persecute his servants as they persecuted him, while others would keep their teaching.
verses.meaning: Followers may share their master’s rejection, while some receive their message. Children should report persecution, bullying, or harm to trusted safe adults rather than endure silently.
verses.prayer: God, protect and strengthen mistreated people.
verses.discussion_question: How can disciples seek safety when mistreated? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Make a family plan for getting help if faith leads to mistreatment.
verses.do_it_today: Review a safe exit-and-tell plan with an adult, or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:20, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But all these things will they do unto you for my name’s sake, because they know not him that sent me.
verses.little_bible: But they will do all these things to you because of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People would mistreat them because they did not know the Father.
verses.meaning: Hostility to disciples arises from rejection of Jesus and ignorance of the Father who sent him. A child must not be told every conflict proves faithful witness.
verses.prayer: Father, help people come to know you.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we avoid calling every disagreement persecution?
verses.family_discussion: List clues that distinguish persecution from correction or disagreement.
verses.do_it_today: Before calling conflict persecution, ask a wise adult for perspective.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:21, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin.
verses.little_bible: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin: but now they have no excuse for their sin.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus’ words exposed sin and removed its excuse.
verses.meaning: Jesus’ coming and speaking brought clearer responsibility by exposing rejection. This does not mean ignorance makes people morally perfect, nor should “guilt” be used to shame a child into disclosure.
verses.prayer: Jesus, bring truthful conviction without shame.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between conviction and shame? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how accountability can tell truth without humiliating someone.
verses.do_it_today: Use the words, “What happened was wrong, but I am not worthless.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:22, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: He that hateth me hateth my Father also.
verses.little_bible: The one who hates me hates my Father also.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Hatred of Jesus also rejects his Father.
verses.meaning: Because Jesus reveals the Father, hatred of the Son also rejects the Father. This theological claim must not fuel contempt or aggression toward people who do not believe.
verses.prayer: Father, help me honor your Son.
verses.discussion_question: How does Jesus connect responses to him and the Father?
verses.family_discussion: Practise disagreeing about belief without hostility.
verses.do_it_today: Choose respectful words for someone who disagrees.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:23, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father.
verses.little_bible: If I had not done among them the works which no one else did, they would not have had sin: but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus’ unique works exposed the guilt of those who hated him.
verses.meaning: Jesus’ unparalleled works increased the responsibility of those who witnessed and rejected them. The verse addresses culpable rejection of revelation, not ordinary doubt or a struggling child’s questions.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me respond honestly to your works.
verses.discussion_question: Why are honest questions different from deliberate rejection?
verses.family_discussion: Welcome an honest question without treating it as rebellion.
verses.do_it_today: Ask one honest question about Jesus without fear of punishment.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:24, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause.
verses.little_bible: But this happens so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: They hated me without a cause.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Their undeserved hatred fulfilled Scripture.
verses.meaning: Jesus locates causeless hatred within Scripture’s pattern of the righteous sufferer. Fulfillment does not make hatred good or mean victims should remain in danger.
verses.prayer: God, stand with people hated without cause.
verses.discussion_question: How can Scripture name unjust hatred without approving it? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Read the cited Psalm context with an older child, or skip.
verses.do_it_today: Make a card affirming someone treated unfairly, with adult help.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:25, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me:
verses.little_bible: But when the Comforter comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceeds from the Father, he will testify of me:
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus sends the Spirit of truth from the Father. The Spirit proceeds from the Father and testifies about Jesus.
verses.meaning: Jesus sends the Spirit from the Father; the Spirit proceeds from the Father and testifies about Jesus. Eastern and Western Christian traditions formulate the Spirit’s eternal procession differently. The verse does not make private voices or impressions unquestionable commands.
verses.prayer: Holy Spirit, testify truly about Jesus.
verses.discussion_question: What does the Spirit’s testimony focus on?
verses.family_discussion: Compare the Spirit’s testimony about Jesus with claims centered on oneself.
verses.do_it_today: Check a claimed message against Scripture with a trusted adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:26, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.

verses.kjv: And ye also shall bear witness, because ye have been with me from the beginning.
verses.little_bible: And you also will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples would testify because they had known Jesus from the beginning.
verses.meaning: The apostles also testify because they accompanied Jesus from the beginning. Their eyewitness role is distinctive; children may speak truthfully about what they learn without claiming apostolic authority.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help us speak truthfully about you.
verses.discussion_question: What made the first disciples special witnesses?
verses.family_discussion: Name ways to report truth accurately without exaggeration.
verses.do_it_today: Retell one fact about Jesus accurately and humbly.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 15:27, Jesus teaching disciples with a grapevine nearby, historically appropriate setting, gentle non-frightening composition, no text.
